destination.name: Mount Kaputar National Park
destination.tagline: Volcanic ranges near Narrabri, with a 1,510 m summit and a rock face of organ-pipe columns.
destination.description: Mount Kaputar National Park surrounds a volcano that was active 17 to 21 million years ago, 50 km east of Narrabri. Erosion has carved the Nandewar Range into lava terraces, volcanic plugs and dykes, and the 1,510 m summit views take in one-tenth of New South Wales. The park shelters bats, wallabies, quolls and bright pink and red slugs that appear after rain.
whyVisit: Walk to Sawn Rocks' organ-pipe cliff
Visit Horton Falls and its rock pools

goodToKnow.title: Slugs after rain
goodToKnow.detail: The red triangle slug and the pink slug are known to appear after rainfall.

goodToKnow.title: May close
goodToKnow.detail: The park is always open but may close at times for poor weather or fire danger.

goodToKnow.title: Easy Sawn Rocks walk
goodToKnow.detail: Sawn Rocks is a 1.5 km return walk beside a creek bed; Horton Falls is about 40 minutes from Barraba.

destination.bestTimeBlurb: Come in {months}: spring and autumn avoid the extremes of a semi-arid inland summer, and rain brings out the park's slugs.
